definitions.explanation: Counting down seconds before an event, such as a rocket launch or New Year's. Also used in shogi/go for time pressure at the end of a game.

examples.japanese: {秒読|びょうよ}みが{始|はじ}まった。
{打|う}ち{上|あ}げの{秒読|びょうよ}みに{入|はい}った。
examples.english: The launch has entered the countdown phase.

examples.japanese: {開幕|かいまく}まであと{三日|みっか}、いよいよ{秒読|びょうよ}みだ。
examples.english: Three days until the opening — the countdown is on.

notes:
Counting down seconds before an event. Used both literally (rocket launches, New Year's) and figuratively (any situation approaching a deadline).

FORMS:
{秒|びょう} (second) + {読|よ}み (reading/counting).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {秒読|びょうよ}みに{入|はい}る: to enter the countdown phase
- {秒読|びょうよ}みが{始|はじ}まる: the countdown begins
- {秒読|びょうよ}み{段階|だんかい}: countdown stage

BOARD GAMES:
In {将棋|しょうぎ} and {囲碁|いご}, {秒読|びょうよ}み refers to the time-pressure phase where a player must move within a set number of seconds. The timekeeper counts aloud.

USAGE:
Often used metaphorically: {閉店|へいてん}の{秒読|びょうよ}みに{入|はい}った (the store has entered the countdown to closing).
